messages:
sam: FYI seeing a big spike in retries for svc/gpu-infer in us-west-2, lots of tokens getting retried and a single pod (gpu-12) is pegged, others idle.

maria_ops: ugh, noticed latency climb around 11:05 UTC too. Any recent drains or updates?

kevin: we did a rolling kernel patch on a couple of nodes earlier, some were cordoned then uncordoned. Could that rebalanced kube-proxy state?

sam: looks like connection counts are uneven on ipvs. netstat shows thousands to gpu-12.

sam: ```
# ipvsadm -Ln --stats | grep gpu-infer
TCP  10.20.30.5:443 rr  Masq    10000  2000  0  0  0  0  0  0  0
-> 10.1.12.24:443     Masq    9500  1900  0  0
-> 10.1.13.11:443     Masq     250  100   0  0
-> 10.1.14.17:443     Masq     250  0     0  0
```

jing-wang: that skew is extreme. Any MTU or RDMA alerts from those nodes? RDMA-enabled nodes should be evenly used.

sam: ping and mtr show intermittent packet loss between gpu-13 and gpu-12, and small MTU mismatch on one host (9000 vs 1500).

maria_ops: oh that could break path MTU/PMTU discovery causing retransmits and ipvs retries. We also saw a few RSTs in the kube-proxy logs.

kevin: I pulled kube-proxy logs from the affected node, there are a bunch of "sync proxy table" warnings and "hash change" messages when the node rejoined.

kevin: ```
I0612 11:05:18.123456  1234 proxysync.go:312] svc/gpu-infer: rebuilding dsts, oldHash=0xdeadbeef newHash=0xbeefdead
W0612 11:05:18.125000  1234 proxysync.go:456] inconsistent endpoint order, rehashing
E0612 11:05:19.200000  1234 proxysync.go:500] failed to sync ipvs scheduler state: conntrack failure: timed out
```

sam: conntrack exhaustion on the host? netstat shows conntrack table near limit on gpu-12.

maria_ops: increase conntrack for now and fix MTU mismatch. That should reduce retries while we stabilize.

oncall: bumped net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max from 262144 to 524288 on gpu-12 and gpu-13 via Ansible, pushed sysctl.

ops-bot: @oncall performed sysctl update on hosts gpu-12,gpu-13 (change: nf_conntrack_max=524288).

jing-wang: also recommend setting IPVS affinity mode to "persistent" temporarily to reduce rehash churn until we fix node flapping. But watch for hotspots.

kevin: temporary mitigation applied: kube-proxy on affected nodes restarted with --ipvs-scheduler=rr --ipvs-sync-period=5s and --ipvs-min-sync-period=10s to smooth rehash.

sam: after conntrack bump + MTU fix + kube-proxy tweak, traffic distribution looks more even. no longer all hitting gpu-12, retries dropped by ~70%.

maria_ops: root cause: node maintenance + MTU mismatch + low conntrack caused ipvs hash churn and failed conntrack entries -> sticky mapping collapsed and traffic condensed on a single backend. We'll add pre-drain checks for MTU/rdma and a kube-proxy restart gating step.

kevin: opened infra ticket INFRA-7234 to add a pre-cordon healthcheck that verifies MTU, RDMA link state, and conntrack headroom before uncordoning.

sam: tagging Customer Success and impacted teams, will monitor for 1h. Thanks all :thumbsup:
